outcome: Breastfeeding practices (initiation time, prelacteal feeding, colostrum provision, artificial feeding)
cohort: The study included 600 mothers admitted in the postnatal ward and mothers attending immunization clinics at Government General Hospital Kurnool, who had children less than 2 years of age.
finding: Various demographic and socio-economic factors, including age, education, occupation, economic status, religion, type of family, type of delivery, and child's gender, were significantly associated with mothers' knowledge, attitude, and practices of breastfeeding.
mod_finding: Mothers who underwent LSCS significantly delayed the initiation of breastfeeding, and the type of delivery was significantly associated with prelacteal feed initiation.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from mothers in the postnatal ward and mothers attending immunization clinics with children less than 2 years of age, between November 2018 and August 2020.
